amendment_filings_source.shape: [{"filing_id": str, "docket": str, "filed_on": str, "effective_date": str, "status": str, "service_class": str, "operation": str, "bracket": {"bracket_id": str, "upper_kwh": int|null, "rate_per_kwh_cents": int}?, "bracket_id": str?, "demand_rate_cents_per_kw": int?, "rationale": str}, ...]

base_tariff_source.shape: {"tariff_id": str, "effective_from": str, "classes": {class: {"brackets": [{"bracket_id": str, "upper_kwh": int|null, "rate_per_kwh_cents": int}, ...], "demand_rate_cents_per_kw": int, "standing_charge_cents_per_day": int}, ...}}

bill_register.container: object keyed by account, each value the array of that account's bill objects

brackets.item_sort: upper_kwh ascending with the unbounded brackets last, ties by bracket_id ascending; a schedule may carry more than one unbounded bracket, or none

schedule_classes.container: object keyed by service class name

exception_queue.container: one compact JSON object per line, json.dumps(..., separators=(',', ':')), each line ended by a newline including the last, and no blank line anywhere

consumption_kwh.input_coercion: int(str(value).strip()); on failure int(float(str(value).strip())); on failure 0; negative results clamp to 0

effective_from.format_note: exactly YYYY-MM-DD and nothing else. The wider forms a permissive ISO parser accepts, such as a compact 20260106 or a week date 2026-W02-1, are not dates here, and neither is a value carrying leading or trailing whitespace: the #TAR-7301 coercions do not name the period dates, so nothing is trimmed before the form is read.

estimated.input_coercion: booleans unchanged; strings true/1/yes after str(...).strip().lower() -> true; other strings -> false; other types -> bool(value)

peak_demand_kw.input_coercion: int(str(value).strip()); on failure int(float(str(value).strip())); on failure 0; negative results clamp to 0

period_end.format_note: exactly YYYY-MM-DD and nothing else. The wider forms a permissive ISO parser accepts, such as a compact 20260106 or a week date 2026-W02-1, are not dates here, and neither is a value carrying leading or trailing whitespace: the #TAR-7301 coercions do not name the period dates, so nothing is trimmed before the form is read.

period_start.format_note: exactly YYYY-MM-DD and nothing else. The wider forms a permissive ISO parser accepts, such as a compact 20260106 or a week date 2026-W02-1, are not dates here, and neither is a value carrying leading or trailing whitespace: the #TAR-7301 coercions do not name the period dates, so nothing is trimmed before the form is read.

read_id.input_coercion: internal whitespace runs collapse to a single space; the collapsed form is the identity a read is deduplicated on and the one reported

meter_read_source.shape: [{"read_id": str, "account": str, "service_class": str, "period_start": str, "period_end": str, "consumption_kwh": int, "peak_demand_kw": int, "estimated": bool, "note": str}, ...]
